$meta.author: Build Agent 1
$meta.figmaPage: Toy Mart BD — Design System › 02 Primitives
executionOrder: 1. Create the two new text styles in newTextStyles FIRST (Latin/Field/Label, Bangla/Field/Label). Nothing below can bind until they exist.
2. Build Input: create the 8 variant frames bottom-up (Field children, then Field, then FieldGroup, then root), combine as variants, then add properties.
4. Add component properties LAST, after the variant set exists, so the single shared default lands on every variant at once.

5. Figma trap (foundations 11.4): resize() resets BOTH sizing modes to FIXED. Resize first, then set primaryAxisSizingMode / counterAxisSizingMode. Doing it the other way locks every field to its min width.
6. Figma trap (foundations 13.3): componentPropertyReferences cannot be set to null or {field: null}. To unbind, deleteComponentProperty.
7. Figma trap (foundations 13): addComponentProperty with type INSTANCE_SWAP wants the icon component's NODE ID, not its key.
layerDescriptorExtensions: maxWidth (TEXT) — Figma text maxWidth in px; used on Label/Text so it wraps instead of overflowing.
minHeight / maxHeight (FRAME) — auto-layout min/max; used on Textarea Field.
primaryAxisAlign / counterAxisAlign (FRAME) — required to place the 14px error icon on line 1 and to top-align the Textarea value.
textAutoResize / textAlign / textAlignVertical / maxLines / truncate (TEXT) — required because truncation is forbidden system-wide (spec 0.7).
why (property) — non-executable rationale; ignore when executing.

components.name: Input
components.description: Single-line form field. State is a variant axis because a form mockup must show a filled field beside an errored field in one static frame and neither is reachable by hovering (spec 3.1). Hover and Focus were REMOVED from the spec's 6-value State axis per binding decision 5: Hover is a one-token stroke override (color/border/default -> color/border/strong) and Focus is focusVisible=true plus a 2px color/border/focus stroke override, so neither earns a variant. Disabled is KEPT on the axis even though decision 5 calls it interaction-only, because it swaps five tokens at once (field fill, stroke, label, value, helper) and an instance-level five-override is the kind of handoff error the axis exists to prevent. Result 4x2=8 variants. No _scrim: darkening a text field would darken the typed value, which is why spec 3.4 renders hover as a border change instead. No _hit44: Field is 44 or 52 tall at FILL width, already over the 44px minimum in both axes (spec 3.8). Stroke align is INSIDE on every state so the 1px -> 1.5px -> 2px changes never move the field's outer box and the form never jumps 0.5px on focus. Error border is red (color/feedback/danger) while the focus ring is teal (color/border/focus), so 'errored' and 'where am I' are never the same hue. The Error node is a permanent layer whose visibility is driven by the variant, not a boolean, so 'State=Default with an error showing' is unreachable. Radius is radius/md (12) per spec; buttons use radius/lg, form controls do not. Every storefront field uses Size=Large (16px) because Android Chrome and iOS Safari zoom the viewport on focus under 16px; Size=Medium (15px) is admin-only.

properties.name: label
properties.why: Same string on all 8 variants, so it is genuinely shared and safe to bind.

properties.name: showLabel
properties.why: Label frame is visible:true on all 8 variants, so a single shared default is correct. A hidden child leaves no auto-layout gap behind. In code the <label> survives as visually-hidden, never dropped.

properties.name: placeholder
properties.why: Characters are shared; only VISIBILITY differs per state and that is left per-variant and unbound.

properties.name: value
properties.why: Characters are shared; visibility differs per state (hidden on Default) and is therefore per-variant, NOT bound.

properties.name: helperText
properties.default: We will SMS your order updates here

properties.name: showHelper
properties.why: Bound to the inner TEXT, not to the Helper frame. The Helper FRAME's visibility varies per variant (false on State=Error) and a property-bound visible would override every variant and show the helper under the error. Helper/Text is visible:true on all 8 variants, so binding there is safe; showHelper=false collapses the HUG frame to zero.

properties.name: prefixSwap
properties.why: Spec 3.2 asks for icon/phone; no phone glyph exists in the 51-icon Phosphor set, so the default falls back to spec 0.9's icon/circle. Accepts an icon or a text chip (e.g. +880) on an instance.

properties.name: focusVisible
properties.why: Uniform false on all 8 variants. Because it is property-bound it cannot be toggled on an instance by hand; use instance.setProperties({focusVisible: true}). Never set it true on State=Disabled (spec 0.4: disabled controls leave the tab order).

components.name: Textarea
components.description: Multi-line form field. Axis shape is deliberately identical to Input (spec 4.1) because the two are reviewed side by side and a different axis shape between them creates handoff mistakes; the same Hover/Focus removal and Disabled retention applies for the same reasons. Field is VERTICAL, counter-axis HUG with a min height per Size (96 / 120) and a max height (240 / 320), so it auto-grows with content and then scrolls, and never shrinks below the min. Value is top-left aligned and multi-line; the Field's counter-axis alignment is MIN (top), not CENTER, which is the only token/layout difference from Input (spec 4.4). Footer is one row holding Message and Counter so a wrapped error and the counter share a baseline. Counter is hidden by default and right aligned; it turns color/feedback/warning at 90% of the limit and color/feedback/danger at 100% as an instance override, not a variant. The .lang-bn build raises min-height to 108 (Medium) and 136 (Large) because Bangla at 15px runs 27.6px per line against 24px Latin, so 96px of box holds only 2.6 Bangla lines (spec 4.6); max-heights are unchanged. Resize is vertical-only in CSS and suppressed under 768px, where auto-grow covers the case.

newTextStyles.name: Latin/Field/Label
newTextStyles.reason: Spec 3.3 requires the field label at 14px / 600. No existing style has that pair: Latin/*/body-sm is 14/400 and Latin/*/label is 13/600. Line-height 150% is body-sm's 1.50 (foundations 5.2); tracking 0 because body-sm's tracking is 0 (label's 0.004em belongs to 13px and is not carried up).

newTextStyles.name: Bangla/Field/Label
newTextStyles.reason: Parallel Bangla style required by spec 0.7 (every Latin text style has a Bangla twin). 173% = body-sm Bangla line-height 1.73 (foundations 5.2 already bakes the x1.15 in). Tracking 0 per the absolute Bangla tracking rule.

notes: AXIS DEVIATION, the big one. Spec 3.1 / 4.1 specify State = Default | Hover | Focus | Filled | Error | Disabled (6x2=12). This manifest ships State = Default | Filled | Error | Disabled (4x2=8), following the deliverable template and binding decision 5. Hover and Focus are dropped because each is a single mechanism already in the system: Hover = override Field.strokeToken to color/border/strong (weight stays 1); Focus = override Field.strokeToken to color/border/focus AND strokeWeight to 2, plus setProperties({focusVisible:true}). Disabled is KEPT against a strict reading of decision 5 because it is a five-token simultaneous swap, which is exactly the handoff error a variant prevents. LEAD DECISION REQUIRED only if you want the 12-variant form back; the layer tree is unchanged either way, so adding Hover and Focus later is a duplicate-and-retoken, not a rebuild.
spacing/N -> space/N throughout. spacing/1=space/1=4, spacing/2=space/2=8, spacing/3=space/3=12, spacing/4=space/4=16.

radius/md is 12 in the real token set, not 10 as spec 3.3 / 4.3 state. Every Field uses the token, so the field radius is 12. _focus corner radius is host + 4 = 16, which is exactly radius/lg — bound as a token, not a raw 16.

TEXT STYLE MAPPING. Value at Size=Medium needs 15/400/160% -> Latin/Mobile/body (15px). Value at Size=Large needs 16/400/160% -> Latin/Desktop/body (16px). This is the one place where the Mobile step is the correct choice for a desktop-named size, and it is because 15px is the mobile floor in foundations 5.2, not because the field is mobile. Helper / Error / Counter are caption 12 -> Latin/Desktop/caption (Mobile and Desktop caption are both 12/500/140%, so Desktop is used per the default mapping rule). Label needs the new Latin/Field/Label — see newTextStyles.

ALTERNATIVE TO THE NEW STYLE, if you want zero new styles: bind Label/Text to the existing Latin/Desktop/label (13 / 600 / 135% / 0.004em), whose stated use in foundations 5.2 is literally 'Form field labels'. That contradicts spec 3.3's explicit 14px. I followed the spec number because 02-primitives says every number in it is final. Your call; it is a one-line swap on 16 layers.

ICON MAPPING. Spec 3.6 rule 5 asks for a 14px alert-triangle; Phosphor has no triangle in the 51-icon set, so Error/_icon is icon/warning-circle at 14x14, coloured with a FILL (color/feedback/danger), never a stroke — Phosphor paths are filled and any leftover Lucide-era stroke override leaves a hairline outline on the glyph. Spec 3.2's prefixSwap default icon/phone does not exist either; it falls back to icon/circle per spec 0.9. suffixSwap default icon/eye exists and is used as specified.

ERROR ATTACHMENT (spec 3.6 / 4.8), expressed in layer names so Code Connect can map it one-for-one. Helper and Error are BOTH permanent layers in Message in every one of the 8 variants; only their visibility changes. That mirrors the markup requirement that the error

is always in the DOM and empty when valid, because a node mounted at validation time is routinely missed by aria-live. Mapping: Label/Text ->

LAYER NAMES ARE PATHS. Names like Label/Text, Value/Placeholder, Helper/Text, Error/Text, Prefix/content are written with a slash to disambiguate for the property bindings, because 'Text' appears under more than one parent. Create the node with ONLY the final segment as its Figma name (Text, Placeholder, content, _icon) so the spec's 'Label › _required' notation and the React mapping still read correctly; the path prefix is addressing for you, not a name.

NO _scrim on either component, deliberately. Spec 0.2 puts _scrim on every interactive primitive, but a scrim over a text field darkens the typed value, and spec 3.4 already renders hover as a border change (color/border/default -> color/border/strong) rather than a darkening. This is why no *-hover colour token exists and none should be invented.

NO _hit44 on either component. Spec 0.8 lists the components that carry it and neither Input nor Textarea is among them: Field is 44 or 52 tall at FILL width, so it clears 44 in both axes with the label's own target additive on top (spec 3.8, 4.7).

DISABLED TOKEN CONFLICT, lead decision. This manifest follows spec 0.4: disabled fill = color/bg/subtle, disabled text = color/text/tertiary, border = 1px color/border/default. The Color collection ALSO contains color/bg/disabled and color/text/disabled, and foundations 3 argues explicitly that color/text/disabled 'must be a separate token rather than a misused tertiary'. I used 0.4 so Input and Textarea match Button and IconButton, which were built from the same rule. If you want to move the whole system to the dedicated tokens, it is a two-token find-and-replace on the Disabled rows here and should be done across all primitives at once, not just these two.

ROOT WIDTH. Spec 3.5 asks for counter axis FILL on the root, which a component set cannot have (there is nothing to fill). Every variant is built FIXED at 320 wide; when placed, set the instance's horizontal sizing to FILL. 320 is the documentation width, not a constraint — the layer tree has no fixed widths other than the 20x20 affix frames.

LABEL WRAPPING. Label is a HORIZONTAL row holding Label/Text then Label/_required with gap space/1 (4) and counter alignment MIN, so the asterisk sits on line 1 when a long Bangla label wraps (spec 3.7: the asterisk stays after the label text in both scripts, and the 8px Label->Field gap is measured from the last line). Label/Text is HUG with maxWidth 300 rather than FILL, because a FILL text would push the asterisk to the far right edge on short labels. maxWidth 300 = 320 root minus the 4px gap and the asterisk's advance, with slack. If you change the documentation width, change maxWidth with it.

NO TRUNCATION ANYWHERE (spec 0.7). Every TEXT layer carries truncate:false. Label wraps to 2 lines max, Helper and Error wrap to 3 lines max, Input's Value is maxLines 1 and never wraps (long Bangla addresses go to Textarea, not Input), Textarea's Value is unbounded. maxLines is recorded as the design intent; do NOT set Figma's truncation on any of them — a truncated Bangla label frequently loses the verb.

MESSAGE ALIGNMENT. Message is VERTICAL with gap 0 holding Helper and Error (exactly one visible per state). The Error row itself is HORIZONTAL with gap space/1 and counter alignment MIN, which is spec 3.5's 'counter alignment Top' — that is what keeps the 14px icon on line 1 of a wrapped three-line Bangla error instead of floating to the vertical centre of the block.

TEXTAREA BANGLA MIN-HEIGHTS. Build two extra documentation instances (not variants) at min-height 108 (Medium) and 136 (Large) for the .lang-bn build, per spec 4.6. In CSS the min-height comes from --textarea-min-h which .lang-bn overrides; max-heights are unchanged at 240 / 320.

TEXTAREA COUNTER THRESHOLDS are instance overrides, not variants: color/text/secondary normally, color/feedback/warning at 90% of the limit, color/feedback/danger at 100%. It is aria-live="polite" and announces at those two thresholds only, never per keystroke.

TEXTAREA DEFAULT CONTENT DEVIATES, intentionally. Spec 4.2 says 'same property set as Input', which taken literally would ship a textarea labelled 'Mobile number'. The property SET is identical; the default STRINGS are the address field, which is what the component is for. helperText is spec 4.8's exact string ('Add a landmark — beside which shop, which floor'), which that section explicitly specifies as a Helper and not an Error because it is guidance present before the user types. errorText is authored by me — the spec gives none — and follows spec 3.6 rule 7: it names the fixable thing and never says 'please'. Replace it if you have a better string; the shape does not change.

NUMERALS are Western 0-9 in both locales, including the Textarea counter and the Input phone value. The font stack must put Hanken Grotesk FIRST so U+0030-0039 resolve Latin and only Bangla glyphs fall through to Anek Bangla. Never list Anek Bangla first.

INTERACTION STATES, the full override recipe for the states board, so none of these get rebuilt as variants later. Hover: Field.strokeToken -> color/border/strong, weight 1. Pressed: not applicable to a text field (no pressed affordance on an input; the caret is the feedback). Focus: Field.strokeToken -> color/border/focus, strokeWeight -> 2, plus setProperties({focusVisible:true}). Error+Focus: keep State=Error (border stays 1.5px color/feedback/danger, the field's own identity) and add the ring via setProperties({focusVisible:true}) — red border, teal ring, two hues, so 'errored' and 'where am I' are never confused. This is the reason color/border/focus is teal and not brand. Disabled: use the variant; never add the ring.

INTERACTIVE SUFFIX is a separate documentation instance named 'Input / interactive suffix', NOT a variant and NOT part of this manifest's 8. When a suffix is interactive (password reveal, clear) it is an IconButton Size=Medium at 44x44 and the Field's padding-right drops to space/1 (4) so the 44px button fits inside a 44px field without the field growing. Spec 3.8 calls this the only case where Field padding changes.

CLIP CONTENT IS FALSE on the root, FieldGroup, Field, Value, Message, Helper, Error and Footer. The _focus ring sits 4px OUTSIDE the Field's bounds, so a single clipping ancestor anywhere in that chain silently eats the ring — this is the defect that made the focus ring invisible on the earlier states board.

MOTION: fast 120ms on the border-colour change, easing standard cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1), wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; reduced-motion fallback is no transition. spring is forbidden here (spec 0.5).
